entries.text: The festival comes once a year, on the night the river runs slowest.
Every family folds a paper lantern, writes a wish on its side, and lets the water carry it away.
I hadn't been back in six years. Then Daichi called.

entries.name: Daichi
entries.text: Come for the lanterns. My cousin is visiting, and she keeps asking about you.
I said I would think about it. I had already bought the ticket.
Three days later, the train left me at the bridge with one bag and no plan.
The river was louder than I remembered.
The festival lanterns were already lit when I reached the river.
You came! I didn't think you would.
Oh, sorry. I'm Hana. Daichi's cousin.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: He said you'd get lost at least twice.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: So I drew you a map.
Only once. Well, twice.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: Oh, and I left something for you, in your game folder. Look in the characters folder.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: That's me in there. hana.chr. Don't open it, it's private.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: ...Huh. Did I just disappear from your folder?

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: There's a copy of me in the files folder. You could put me back, if you like.
I wasn't sure what she meant. I let her go on anyway.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: Never mind. A new game always brings me back.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: I can see more from in here than you think, friend.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: ...Sorry. That wasn't me. Was it?
Paper lanterns drifted past us one by one, each carrying somebody's wish downstream.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: Did you write one? Everybody writes one. But first, a fortune.
"One fortune, one hundred yen," the stall keeper said.
The slip stuck to its neighbor, and I had to peel them apart.
I unrolled the paper and read it twice: great luck.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: Great luck! See? The river likes you.
"Three hundred yen," the stall keeper said. "Wishes are extra."
"Unless you can find the pairs," she added, and turned a row of paper lanterns face down.
"Only 9 turns? Sharp eyes," the stall keeper said. "Your wish is free."

I took the red one. It glowed like a coal in my hands.
"Candles are in the shed, if you want your lantern to last," the stall keeper said, and nodded at a door behind the stall.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: Oh. You bought one. That's... nice.
The old footbridge creaked under the crowd. Halfway across, Daichi leaned on the rail and watched the water.

entries.name: Daichi
entries.text: There you are. Hana's been looking for you all evening.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: I have not. I've been looking for a good spot to let the lanterns go.
That wasn't what Daichi had said on the phone.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: That's my map! Where did you...
Her handwriting, in the corner: when my train got in.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: Fine. Maybe I asked about you. Twice.

entries.name: Daichi

entries.name: Daichi

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: I can hear you, you know.

entries.name: Daichi
entries.text: The fireworks don't start for a while. Ask me anything.

entries.name: Daichi
entries.text: Then this is it. Nobody else ever thinks of the middle of the bridge.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: Write your wish on the side first. Only three words: the paper is small.

entries.name: Daichi
entries.text: Fireworks and friends, I bet. That's my kind of wish.
We set the lantern on the water together. It turned once, as if to look back at us, and its little flame burned blue.

entries.name: Daichi
entries.text: Make a wish. The shrine writes them as {name}: {wish}. They're free on this side of the stall.

entries.name: Hana

Below us, the river carried the last of the lights out of sight.

entries.name: Hana
entries.text: Same time next year?
Before I could answer, the first firework burst over the river, and Hana laughed.
I nodded. The lanterns were gone, but none of us moved to leave.
The last train leaves at ten. Hana was watching the water.
